prompt: Ọdang kuwa ya ombli
solution0: Ee lẹ abali yila flefle, lẹ ọtunu fla bonu. Ee bi aya nee yila chẹẹ ee le ta ombli, ọnda mla ukpamu.
solution1: Ee lẹ abali yila flefle, lẹ ọtunu kla bonu. Ee bi aya nee yila chẹẹ ee le ta ombli, ọnda mla ukpamu.
gemini_translated0: When a famine came to the land they were very hungry, and they had nothing to eat. They saw someone with a small piece of yam, he had some ukpamu.
gemini_translated1: The time you eat food is in the early morning, and your mouth will be fresh. If you wait until it is too late before you eat, it comes with ukpamu.

prompt: Ọchẹ ga lẹ ihi pa ọla
solution0: Lẹ ọla tugwo no le kpla, a kwu ihi chọ taapu taapu, a gee họi pia ihi eyi tọla. O kwu je, a lọ pẹ, lọ bẹ tu ogo. A chẹ, a le mla ikpẹpi.
solution1: Lẹ ọla tugwo no le kpla ẹẹn, a kwu ihi chọ taapu taapu, a gee họi pia ihi eyi tọla. O kwu je, a lọ pẹ, lọ bẹ tu ogo. A chẹ, a le mla ikpẹpi.
gemini_translated0: A person is going to eat pounded yam. When the yam is ready to be pounded, you cut the yam into small pieces, then you wash the pieces of yam. After washing, you put it in the pot, then you put it on the fire. When it is done, you eat it with *ikpẹpi*.
gemini_translated1: When a person wants to prepare pounded yam, after the yam is cooked and done, you pound the yam very well, then you cut the yam that is pounded. When it is finished, you dish it, and dish it into the mortar. Then you can eat it with *ikpẹpi* soup.

prompt: Abọ Idọma ge bi ọnya nyọ ọlẹ ọba lẹ a
solution0: Ọdang kee lije kpo tọ ọba kpẹm, ẹnẹnu lẹ ohoọba la luwo. Anchọnya kọ ọnya mla aanya ku ipọma ọladanu ge bi ọnya ta ga ọlẹ ọyanu a.
solution1: Ọdang kee lije kpo tọ ọnya kpẹm, ẹnẹnu lẹ ohoọba la luwo. Anchọnya kọ ọnya mla aanya ku ipọma ọladanu ge bi ọnya ta ga ọlẹ ọbunu a.
gemini_translated0: The Idoma people have their king, but if the Ogbadibo person were to become king, tears would not cease flowing from the eyes of the king's family. Some people and their children in the community have become a burden to their family.
gemini_translated1: An Idoma person is a person who fears God, and if you see them, they are very peaceful. A person who is a person with a good heart is a person of God.

prompt: Ọdi wẹ eku ku enkpo mla ẹgọ
solution0: Ee ge bi enkpo mla ẹgọ gba ọda alẹwa lẹbẹ ku abahi mla akeyi. Gbọbu ka gba, a lẹ enkpo mla ẹgọ na ohigwu ọnjẹ.
solution1: Ee ge bi entu mla ẹgọ gba ọda alẹwa lẹbẹ ku abahi mla akeyi. Gbọbu ka gba, a lẹ enkpo mla ẹgọ na ohigwu ọnjẹ.
gemini_translated0: There is a way of sharing *enkpo* and *ẹgọ*. They use *enkpo* and *ẹgọ* to create beautiful designs on calabash and pots. After it is created, the *enkpo* and *ẹgọ* are washed off with food water.
gemini_translated1: It is said that Rat put *enkpo* and money. They were going to use the *entu* and money to marry a beautiful woman and put her in a room and kitchen. For that reason, they put the *enkpo* and money on top of the food.

prompt: Eko na ọya fiiajẹ otu abọ anyakwọchẹ gee gbọ ọcha lẹ a
solution0: Ogbọ kọ ọcha dooduma wẹ ọcham ta kpa kpa kpa
solution1: Ogbọ kọ ọka dooduma wẹ ọcham ta kpa kpa kpa
gemini_translated0: The *eko* and vegetable soup that Anayakwoche's group used one hand to eat at the farm was very white and my own was making a 'kpa kpa kpa' sound.
gemini_translated1: The *eko* and soup that that one-armed woman sells by the Ogbọ market makes a sound like kpa kpa kpa when she eats corn.

solution0: A lẹ akeyi amang kẹẹ abahi gba, lọ da mla enkpọ no okwọla lọhilọhin chẹẹ a lọ hẹ tu enkpọhọ ne chọla gbọbu ka kpo ọdọhọ ohile tọ.
solution1: A lẹ akeyi amang kẹẹ abahi gba, lọ da mla enkpọ okwọla lọhilọhi chẹẹ a lọ hẹ tu enkpọhọ ne chọla gbọbu ka kpo ọdọhọ ohile tọ.
gemini_translated0: When the time comes that women see themselves as complete human beings, they will, with their different talents, be able to do great things that will move the world forward.
gemini_translated1: When he came with his friends and found them well, he also brought various kinds of gifts and gave them to those he was supposed to give something to according to tradition.

prompt: Ọlẹchẹ ge la anu foofunung
solution0: Ohigbu ọma achẹ lẹ ọlẹ gwo ipọlẹ mla ọmpa uwa, ee kwu pia ugbọga ge le mla ogwa tọha.
solution1: Ohigbu ọma achẹ lẹ ọlẹ gwo ipọlẹ mla ọmpa uwa, ee kwu pia aladogbe ge le mla ogwa tọha.
gemini_translated0: A certain person in the early morning took his child to go and pound yam with a mortar in your house, and also cut a certain bunch of palm fruit with a long cutlass.
gemini_translated1: The Oloche is at the Ohigbu shrine of his fathers where he is performing the ipọlẹ with the ọmpa uwa, he is also clearing a new farmland with the ogwa.

prompt: Ẹgẹẹnya ne ge nya epu ichonklo a
solution0: A lẹ ebu a na kwọ kpo tu ombli ko wlaelu, a lẹ akọkọ mla okpehe gba kwọ pia tu epu a chẹẹ a lẹ ọma futọ ka kwọ nya tọha.
solution1: A lẹ epu a na kwọ kpo tu ombli ko wlaelu, a lẹ akọkọ mla okpehe gba kwọ pia tu epu a chẹẹ a lẹ ọma futọ ka kwọ nya tọha.
gemini_translated0: Their traditional food which is pounded yam, is eaten with Ogbono soup that is drawn, and it is also eaten with chicken and okpehe that they will use to prepare the soup which will enable the pounded yam to go down well.
gemini_translated1: A proverb says one hand cannot lift a load onto the head, but it takes the left and the right hand together to lift a load to the head so that the person can go on a journey.

prompt: Ẹgẹẹnya nee ge ya ibẹ ku ihi lẹ a
solution0: A lẹ ihi pẹ, lọ fu enkpọ ofu ẹchi ẹta, a lọ ta bẹchẹ ko nmo chẹẹ a lọ gba.
solution1: A lẹ ihi pẹ, lọ fu enkpọ okwọla ẹchi ẹta, a lọ ta bẹchẹ ko nmo chẹẹ a lọ gba.
gemini_translated0: This Ẹgẹẹnya went to the farm to tap ihi and after he finished tapping the ihi, he took three calabashes of ofu, and he said that he should be given his own so he could go.
gemini_translated1: Before they could find a reason, He gave them a three-day holiday, and they were told to come with whatever they had.

prompt: Ọdi na alẹchẹ chika o gba ọwọ kuwa
solution0: Ọchẹ kwu ẹbẹ no lẹ ọnyi le inalegwu ta, kwu ẹbẹ a họkọ, lẹ oyi kunu pia kla ikplẹyi ekwu ku ọwọnu. O kwu ẹbẹ a he lachẹ kee le.
solution1: Ọchẹ kwu ẹbẹ no lẹ ọnying le inalegwu ta, kwu ẹbẹ a họkọ, lẹ oyi kunu pia kla ikplẹyi ekwu ku ọwọnu. O kwu ẹbẹ a he lachẹ kee le.
gemini_translated0: It was in the morning that he gave thanks to God, saying where he took the inalegwu from, and how he prepared it, that he brought it and placed it in the center of the mat. He said how they would eat it.
gemini_translated1: This is the story of how he paid homage to God and told him where the *inalegwu* spirit spoke from, told him where they met, and he poured out the *ikplẹyi ekwu* for him. He told him where they would meet again.

prompt: Eko ọnọ na achẹ gbo bla ihi nma ẹhọ a
solution0: Ee le ihi kpo tu ukpamu mla ẹkpa le bi gọlẹ, e lihi a pla bajẹ inu achi. Ọma na achẹ ge tu ili oofu tinu a.
solution1: Ee le ihi kpo tu ukpamu mla ẹkpa le bi gọlẹ, e lihi a pla bajẹ inu achi. Ọma na achẹ ge tu ihi oofu tinu a.
gemini_translated0: There was a woman who prepared Eko with yams in it. When she brought out the yams with a spoon and bag to share, the children broke the pot. She plans to cook white rice.
gemini_translated1: This is the time we plant and the yam does well in the farm. When you harvest the yam and prepare *ukpamu* with *ẹkpa* that is well-prepared, it is very delicious in the mouth. It makes one want to eat white yam every day.

prompt: Ọdang kẹẹ achọnya gaa he ọhọ okoho
solution0: Ee lẹ ọchi okoho a pẹ, kwọ tayila flifli, lẹ enkpọ okwọla hẹtọ kwọ kla che. O họyẹẹ, ee kwọ a da mla abọ. Enyi nee pii tu okoho nee gi pia tu ọhọ a
solution1: Ee lẹ ọchi okoho a pẹ, kwọ tayila flifli, lẹ enkpọ okwọla hẹtọ kwọ kla che. O họyẹẹ, ee kwọ a da mla abọ. Enyi nee pii nma okoho nee gi pia tu ọhọ a
gemini_translated0: When it is time for the women to go to the farm, they will start the farm work, make the mounds, and clear the surroundings. After that, they will plant with their hands. Those who weed the farm will also clear it.
gemini_translated1: When the women go to the farm, after they have harvested the corn, they cut the cornstalks and leave the waste on the ground for it to rot. Then, they will burn it with fire. The smoke from the corn farm will then billow up.

prompt: Ẹgẹẹnya ne achẹ gee gwiye ọkpa ajidọma a
solution0: Ajidọma ọkpa na alọ ge gwiye a. A liye wu enyi ligi wai lukwọ mla isoso nya iye. A logo hẹ enkpọ ta kliye. O fọtu a lẹ agwa ta.
solution1: A ga gwiye ọkpa ajidọma, a liye wu enyi ligi wai lukwọ mla isoso nya iye. A logo hẹ enkpọ ta kliye. O fọtu a lẹ ọwi ta.
gemini_translated0: Long ago, our fathers used to dance one ajidọma, the one ajidọma that we dance. They would put on raffia skirts with isoso on their legs. They would hold something in their hands. It will be in their body.
gemini_translated1: Long ago, when our people would go on an *ajidọma*, they would go with a horse along with their provisions. They would go with something to eat. They did not go empty-handed.

prompt: Abọ ee ge ya ufie oogwu ẹbẹ lẹ a
solution0: Ọchẹ gaa ya ufie, o epali cha bajẹ, o bi ukwuayiga lẹ apunu fa bonu. O kwu ẹwa chẹẹ o lẹ ufie a kla eyeyeye.
solution1: Ọchẹ gaa ya ufie, o ikpali cha bajẹ, o bi ukwuayiga lẹ apunu fa bonu. O kwu ẹwa chẹẹ o lẹ ufie a kla eyeyeye.
gemini_translated0: No matter how much wealth and riches a person has from God, if it is not accompanied by good character and humility, it is all for nothing.
gemini_translated1: When his hand makes a bad charm or when a King makes a charm, it will spoil the *ikpali*, it will bring *ukwuayiga* for the mouth that speaks it. He said that is why his charm is so very powerful.

prompt: Ẹkaoogwa ge lẹ ẹdẹdọ nma ipọlẹ eyi gọ ọha.
solution0: A gaa gwa ẹka, a leyi kwọ hi kwu enuwọ, a lẹ inalegwu ta chẹẹ a lẹ ẹka a tu okonu.
solution1: A gaa cha ẹka, a leyi kwọ hi kwu enuwọ, a lẹ inalegwu ta chẹẹ a lẹ ẹka a tu okonu.
gemini_translated0: The washing of hands is more important than the multitude of people that eat the food. When you want to wash your hands, you don't just dip your fingers in the water, you wash them thoroughly with inalegwu so that when you put your hands in your mouth, it will be clean.
gemini_translated1: *Ẹkaoogwa* is like the story of the tortoise that went to a public gathering. When they shared the corn, it was not enough to go around, and the *inalegwu* said that they should add the corn to make it swell.

prompt: Ọdi wẹ okpapka ka aba yọ lẹ
solution0: Ohi na chika ochilọ a wẹ obọbi no, a lọfu chẹ kum gbẹhi ẹẹ
solution1: Ohi na chika ochilọ a wẹ obọbi no, a lọfu chẹ kum nẹhi ẹẹ
gemini_translated0: This is the maize that Ohi, who is very beautiful, came and bought completely.
gemini_translated1: It is said that the corn that the Spirit ate to the fullest and threw away is what the monkey is now picking to eat.

prompt: Ipu uchulu ku Idọma alekwu leyi alẹwa

gemini_translated0: In the olden days of the Idoma people, this beautiful *Alekwu*. *Alekwu* is the hand that gathers, it is also the broom that sweeps. *Alekwu* is the land that the ancestors left behind.
gemini_translated1: In Idoma tradition, the Alekwu masquerade is beautiful. The Alekwu is the hand that gives, and it is also the mouth that eats. Alekwu is the land that the ancestors own.

prompt: Okwu gekwu ee ge lọ che itakpa gbọbu kee jọ nyi

solution1: Eko na achi a chọgba a, achọnya gee bẹchẹ bai chilẹwu. Achohi ge bai tẹhọ fu ọmapu uwa no bu ekwu a.
gemini_translated0: The matter that will be said has reached the point of *itakpa* because of what happened in Lagos, and for this matter, we are looking for those who will stand as witnesses. We want those who will tell the truth about this situation.
gemini_translated1: The matter to be discussed is that going to check the *itakpa gbọbu* that is bad in Lagos in this government's tenure, the person seeking it will not see it to buy. The person selling it will not even bring it out to the public for the people of the world because of this matter.

prompt: Ọdi na Idọma gee ya mla ọba a
solution0: Ipu ọba na achidọma ge kpo ọdẹhọ lẹbẹkẹ ku iwgu, eye tukpla eje tu ọdang ke kwọ che nma ẹhọ a.
solution1: Ipu ajẹ na achidọma ge kpo ọdẹhọ lẹbẹkẹ ku iwgu, eye tukpla eje tu ọdang ke kwọ che nma ẹhọ a.
gemini_translated0: It is said in Idoma that the king of Ipu, the king of the Idoma people, will name a child *lẹbẹkẹ* when he is born, even if he will later become a thief.
gemini_translated1: This Idoma story is about the queen of Ipu ajẹ, and how the Idoma people would pound ọdẹhọ in a mortar, and when it is ready, dish it into a calabash to present to the husband.

prompt: Ọchẹ le tanyila abo ga ya lẹ a
solution0: A lẹ tanyila ẹga ku ọmpa awọ, a le yẹ tu ẹginu, lẹ abọ kwu ajẹ ko kwu yẹhi.
solution1: A lẹ tanyila ẹga ku ọmpa awọ, a le yẹ tu ẹginu, lẹ ikpo kwu ajẹ ko kwu yẹhi.
gemini_translated0: A person who puts their hand into something that isn't their business and puts their leg on a thorny path, and sees something terrifying, whose hand is that of a witch, it will not be good for them.
gemini_translated1: A person who points a finger at another person, and points with the other five, and also looks at the ground, if a ghost does not kill a witch, a witch does not die.

gemini_translated0: The Idoma say that it is the way of all people that it is one person who starts a matter before others join in.
gemini_translated1: The Idoma have a saying that it is the stomach that tells the mouth to speak one thing after another.

prompt: Agba nya nee ta kla Ọchidọma a
solution0: Ichagba ku Ọchidọma wẹ agaba-idu. Anu foofunu nee ge ta agba ọma ajidọma a

gemini_translated0: This is the reign of the Ọchidọma and Ichagba, the Ọchidọma is the agaba-idu. May this New Year be a good one for the people.
gemini_translated1: This great leader that wears the crown of Ọchidọma and Ichagba is the Ọchidọma, the lion of the tribe. All of you will see a good leader among his people.

prompt: Enyi wẹ eje na achẹ je kwu Idọma
solution0: Ọpu ku Idọma ohima ge hi enyi le ko umu amang ogwo. A lẹ igwu fenyi le gba mla ẹdẹ, a lẹ odugba a wula mla enkpọ okwọla chẹẹ a lẹ ẹdẹ a hogodo pia tọ jaa ọchi no kwu hilando.
solution1: Ọpu ku Idọma ohima ge hi enyi le ko umu amang ogwo. A lẹ igwu fenyi le gba mla ẹdẹ, a lẹ odugba a wula mla enkpọ onmofu chẹẹ a lẹ ẹdẹ a hogodo pia tọ jaa ọchi no kwu hilando.
gemini_translated0: We are the ones who rule from Idọma Ọpu to Idọma Ohima and we give birth to twelve children. We have the igwu that we dance with the ẹdẹ, we have the odugba we use with the enkpọ okwọla then we have the ẹdẹ we beat until it reaches the white man's land.
gemini_translated1: We are the ones who rule Idoma Ọpu and Idoma ohima, that is why we give birth to children on earth. We have clothes that we wear with beads, we have odugba that we mix with onmofu herbs, and we have the beads we use to beautify the tree that is in the farmland.

prompt: Abọ ee gee nu ifu nma ọlẹ lẹ a
solution0: Achẹ gaa nu ifu nma ọlẹ, ee lọfu lukpa tajẹ ọwẹ nee je ki ifu ge yẹ a. Eko na ifu kwuinya wa ga yẹ, ukpa gee jọ kwu.
solution1: Achẹ gaa nu ifu nma ọlẹ, ee lọfu lukpa tajẹ ọwẹ nee je ki ifu ge yẹ a. Eko na ifu gwuta wa ga yẹ, ukpa gee jọ kwu.
gemini_translated0: On one hand, there is that good side that Achẹ has, and on the other hand, there is a bad side that makes people not like them. Wherever there is much goodness, there will also be some badness.
gemini_translated1: Whether you are in the good stomach of Aché or you are in the good stomach of Aché, you love eating ukpa so that the stomach will see it. The moment the stomach sees it, the ukpa is finished.

prompt: Abọ okoho ge gwo ọlẹ lẹ a
solution0: Ọdang ka okoho ga gwo ọlẹ, o bi ọkọ kunu lẹ achi kpo go ẹga no dọka chẹẹ o lẹ ọlunu ta lọlọhi
solution1: Ọdang ka okoho ga gwo ọlẹ, o bi elu kunu lẹ achi kpo go ẹga no dọka chẹẹ o lẹ ọlunu ta lọlọhi.
gemini_translated0: The way he cooked the okoho soup, even if Ọdang were to cook the soup, he would start a fire and go somewhere else just to see that it has a delicious taste.
gemini_translated1: The chicken's hand that washed the plate and Odan's hand that also washed the plate, they collaborated so that they can go to the place where it is very delicious.

prompt: Ọdang ka gaa ya anọ ene
solution0: A lẹ ikpali ẹno tanọ cha, a lọ kpo tu ẹhi chọla. A ge be piọ eyi mla ochupẹ jaa gbeko ne anọ bẹchẹ.
solution1: A lẹ epali ẹno tanọ cha, a lọ kpo tu ẹhi chọla. A ge be piọ eyi mla ochupẹ jaa gbeko ne anọ bẹchẹ.
gemini_translated0: When it gets to the time that people have finished eating ikpali in the afternoon, they will then go and rest. They will be drinking water with ochupẹ that was used to cook.
gemini_translated1: When it comes to those people, once they finish eating their epali, they will clean their hands. They will then cook food with ochupẹ in the pot for those at home.

prompt: Ọdi wẹ oya ogbubita ajidọma a
solution0: Ogbubita wẹ uchẹ ku ọkaooda mla ohioochila. Ọchẹ no gaa dọka ko gbubita, chẹẹ achẹ ọha chẹ amẹ
solution1: Ogbubita wẹ uchulu ku ọkaooda mla ohioochila. Ọchẹ no gaa dọka ko gbubita, chẹẹ achẹ ọha chẹ amẹ
gemini_translated0: This is the suffering of an Ogbubita from Ajidọma and Ogbubita is the route to ọkaooda and ohioochila. A person who wants to be an Ogbubita must first cross a river.
gemini_translated1: This is the story of ogbubita of Idoma and Ogbubita is the leader of ọkaooda and ohioochila. The person who goes to the place to gbubita, that is the person they call the one.

prompt: Gbọbu ku ọchẹ ko gwọla eyinya duuma
solution0: O lẹ ewo gwu nma ikpo achọla le pia bonu, lẹ ẹwu gwo kwọha chẹẹ kwu enkpọ hẹ kwọ
solution1: O lẹ ewo gwu nma ikpo achọla le pia bonu, lẹ ẹwu gwo kwọha chẹẹ kwu ọla hẹ kwọ
gemini_translated0: Everyone from the throne praised the horse greatly. He took a goat for the *achọla* people who came, and the cloth he used to tie it is still on it.
gemini_translated1: Gbọbu took a stool and bought one horse. He has an *ewo* that was sewn with *ikpo achọla* thread, and the *ẹwu* is very beautiful to look at.

prompt: Idọma ge kwita kahini eko nẹ ẹhi ge kwu a ọchẹduu ii po no
solution0: Eko nẹ ọji gbọ oopa chẹẹ odunduu achẹ gbo kẹla.
solution1: Eko nẹ ọji gbọ oowu chẹẹ odunduu achẹ gbo kẹla.
gemini_translated0: An Idoma person believes that the eko that the spirit has wrapped is not removed from the eko that a fly has perched on, because a big trouble is better than a small one.
gemini_translated1: An Idoma person believes that if a ghost kills a person, it does not take long before the deceased’s relative also dies mysteriously.

prompt: Ugwu no che ẹyi iho O ge je ẹjẹn
